extracted.intended_audience: public relations students and practitioners (PR professionals crafting press releases)
extracted.subtask_description: Using Grunig & Hunt's four-model typology to evaluate or craft press releases so as to maximize media pickup while managing credibility cost. Focuses on one-way vs two-way and asymmetric vs symmetric communication postures applied to release content and disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press agentry / publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: One-way; persuasion-only; accuracy not a priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release seeks attention by spectacle (a stunt, an exaggerated claim). High initial pickup risk on tabloid/entertainment beats; low credibility carry-over and burns the source's repeat-pickup capacity. Anti-pattern: presenting spectacle as factual reporting; likely to be flagged as PR-bait and demoted by quality outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release reports facts (financial result, appointment, study release) without audience tailoring or feedback. Picks up reliably on dedicated business/science wires; weak on consumer or political beats. Requirement: include key data and source documents to avoid slipping into press-agentry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-way asymmetric
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-way; persuasion-driven; audience research used to change the public, not the organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release is pre-tested for which framing will most move readers. High pickup on issues the audience already cares about; moderate credibility risk. Transparency guidance: disclose sponsor's stake in the outcome to reduce credibility cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-way symmetric
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-way; mutual-adjustment posture; the release reflects audience input back into organisational behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pickup is steady across reputable beats; highest credibility carry-over and best long-run journalist relationships. Markers include cited public input, acknowledgment of opposing concerns, and admissions of uncertainty; referencing actual adjustments signals this posture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication model dimensions (one-way vs two-way; asymmetric vs symmetric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify the release along two dimensions: directionality (one-way vs two-way) and intent (asymmetric persuasion vs symmetric mutual adjustment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These dimensions predict both likely pickup patterns and long-run credibility costs. Use the classification to anticipate which outlets will be receptive and how repeat-pickup capacity may be affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-fit honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release acknowledge — even implicitly — which model it is operating under?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press-agentry releases that 'pretend' to be public-information releases damage source trust. Evaluate for deceptive posture (e.g., spectacle disguised as neutral reporting). Honesty about intent reduces long-run credibility loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetric-model markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release show evidence of dialogue (cited public input, acknowledgment of opposing concerns, plain admission of uncertainty)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These markers signal symmetric practice and increase pickup on civic/accountability beats. Examples: quoting stakeholder feedback, noting tradeoffs, describing consultation processes. Absence of such markers suggests less credible or one-way posture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of pure publicity stunts
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases positioned in pure press-agentry mode are likely to be flagged by quality outlets as PR-bait and demoted in routine channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid spectacle, exaggerated claims, or gimmicks presented as substantive news. If a stunt is used, clearly separate promotional elements from factual disclosure to reduce risk of demotion and credibility loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-information completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: For factual releases, are the key data, methodology, and source documents attached?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-information mode requires substantive disclosure (e.g., data, methods, documents) or it slides into press agentry. Scoring guidance: completeness of attachments and transparency of methods increases pickup on business/science wires and credibility with reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymmetric persuasion transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: If the release is two-way asymmetric (issue advocacy), does it disclose its sponsor's stake in the outcome?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about sponsorship and interests mitigates credibility risk. Anti-pattern: targeted persuasion without disclosure, which can boost short-term pickup but harm long-run relationships with reputable outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetric-mode revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release reference adjustments the issuer has made in response to public input?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly noting changes made because of public feedback signals symmetric-model practice and earns pickup on civic/accountability beats. Example: describing policy or product modifications prompted by consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence-theory marker
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release suggest the issuer integrates communication with management decisions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per Grunig's 'excellence study,' PR units that practice symmetric communication are correlated with positive organizational outcomes. Releases that indicate integration of communication into management signal higher organizational maturity and are associated with better long-run pickup and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pickup-worthiness by outlet type
rubrics_metrics.description: Different outlet types prefer different postures: reputable national and specialty outlets favor public-information and symmetric releases; trade and entertainment outlets pick up press-agentry pieces more readily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use expected outlet preferences to target distribution. Note trade-off: press-agentry may yield immediate visibility on entertainment/tabloid beats but compounds credibility cost; symmetric/public-information favours sustained pickup across reputable beats.
